item.title: AWS launches Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments for AI agent transaction automation
item.description:
AWS launches Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments for AI agent transaction automation

When an AI agent accesses a paid resource, the server returns HTTP 402 Payment Required. AWS now offers a managed way for agents to handle that payment automatically.

🔍 Overview

  • Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments handles machine‑to‑machine payment workflows on behalf of the agent.
  • The x402 protocol is an open standard for HTTP‑based machine‑to‑machine payments.
  • Integrated with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments, the service discovers, accesses, and pays for APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and web content autonomously.

🧩 How it works

  1. An agent running in Anchor Browser makes a request (e.g., fetching a premium research report or calling a paid data‑enrichment API).
  2. The server responds with HTTP 402 Payment Required together with the amount, accepted payment methods, and a payment address.
  3. AgentCore payments detects and parses the 402 challenge, distinguishes it from other 4xx errors, and constructs the correct payment header with the required cryptographic proof.
  4. The payment is processed through the x402 protocol; the original request is resubmitted with the payment header while preserving session state, cookies, and request context.
  5. The transaction is authorized and completed within the agent’s configured budget, and observability data (attempts, approvals, denials, settlements) is sent to Amazon CloudWatch.

⚙️ Key details

Component Role
Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments Cloud‑based browser automation purpose‑built for AI agents; manages authentication, navigation, network capture, and live view
x402 protocol Open standard for HTTP‑based machine‑to‑machine payments
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments Fully managed capability that manages wallet connectivity, enforces configurable spending limits, processes x402 payments, and provides audit logs

Additional capabilities

  • Supports multiple payment schemes (exact, up‑to, and protocol variants) without hard‑coding vendor logic.
  • Maintains compatibility across x402 merchant implementations that may differ in challenge format, supported stablecoins, or settlement timing.
  • Stores a private key for signing payments, with secure key storage, key rotation, credential refresh, and provider failover.
  • Enforces per‑session and per‑transaction spend limits with real‑time budget tracking across concurrent agent executions.
  • Captures every payment attempt, approval, denial, and settlement in audit logs for compliance and reconciliation.
  • Provides idempotency, essential for wallet operations.

🚀 Availability

  • Developed in collaboration with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory.
  • The solution is now available on AWS Marketplace.

💡 Why it matters

  • Without a managed payment service, an agent would need to internalize the entire payment stack, including secure key management and budget enforcement.
  • Browser‑based agents have the additional constraint that payment must occur within the same browser session; the integrated service satisfies this requirement automatically.
  • Built‑in observability and spending limits help operators maintain control and compliance while allowing AI agents to autonomously access paid APIs and content.

#AWS #AIAgents #MachineToMachinePayments #CloudAutomation

Source: Building agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments | Amazon Web Services

item.title: xAI launches Grok Bot: persistent AI agents for multi-step tasks
item.description:
xAI launches Grok Bot: persistent AI agents for multi-step tasks

xAI recently launched Grok Bot, a system of always-on AI agents that run on dedicated cloud computers instead of a user’s laptop.

🔍 Overview

Grok Bot is not a chat window. Each Bot runs on its own persistent cloud computer with a real browser, file system, and terminal, plus its own logins to the tools it needs. You assign a role—email, LinkedIn outreach, research, scheduling—and the Bot keeps working after you close the app. Multiple Bots can coordinate on the same task, sharing files, browser sessions, and context through the same cloud infrastructure.

🧩 How it works

  • Each Bot gets a dedicated cloud machine with a browser, file system, and terminal, plus tool logins.
  • Bots continue running after you close the app or laptop lid because they run on cloud infrastructure.
  • You can create 2–6 Bots in a group chat and @-mention new ones mid-conversation; they message each other, pass tasks, and share context without manual relay.
  • A Bot operates its browser and terminal like a person: clicking, typing, navigating, and running commands in the same apps a human would use.
  • Grok Bot connects to structured tools through connectors, plugins, and MCP servers, so it is not limited to xAI’s native integrations.
  • You can record a browser workflow once in screen-recording mode; the Bot learns the sequence from the recording and can replay it later.

⚙️ Key details

  • Roles and tasks: Assign a role and task the same way you would brief a new hire; the Bot uses its cloud machine to complete the work.
  • Hand-offs and coordination: Multiple Bots can work together on the same task, sharing files, browser sessions, and context through the shared cloud infrastructure.
  • Approval gates: Require explicit approval before a Bot sends a message, publishes content, deletes data, makes a purchase, or changes a production system.
  • Recurring routines: Use a routines panel to schedule daily or weekly runs of a task so the Bot checks something without re-prompting.
  • Reusable skills: A process that worked once can be saved as a reusable skill with steps, decision rules, output requirements, and approval boundaries.

🚀 Availability

  • Platforms: Download the app for macOS, Windows, Linux, or iOS and complete the sign-in flow.
  • Account access: Before creating a Bot, pick which accounts it can reach from a list including Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, Salesforce, Microsoft 365, LinkedIn, Zoom, GitHub, Jira, Figma, HubSpot, Canva, and more.
  • Templates: Grok Bot suggests ready-made templates such as a feedback-clustering Bot, an overnight Bot that preps a morning digest, or an inbox-triage Bot.
  • Pricing: Three paths are available—
    • Free trial (card required to start; not charged unless you subscribe),
    • Pro+ at $60/month,
    • Link an existing SuperGrok Heavy or SuperGrok Plus subscription (included at no extra charge once linked).

💡 Why it matters

Grok Bot shifts AI from chat-based assistants to persistent, multi-step agents that can operate continuously and coordinate across tools without constant supervision. Because each Bot runs on dedicated cloud infrastructure, it can handle long jobs, share context with teammates, and respect approval boundaries before taking sensitive actions.

#xAI #GrokBot #AIagents #cloudautomation #workflowautomation

Source: Grok Bot Review: What It Is, Pricing, Features, and How to Use It
